content.title: Justin Bieber is a Coachella regular. Now's the right time to headline
content.text: Updated April 9, 2026, 11:49 a.m. PTAs the start of Coachella 2026 draws near, many attendees are eagerly anticipating the return of one artist: Justin Bieber.When the pop star was announced as a headliner back in September, it drew a number of reactions. For many, it was thrilling because he's never been a billed performer on the lineup, previously only showing up as an attendee or special guest. It's also hard to believe it's his first Coachella set considering he was everywhere in the 2010s with hits such as "Baby," "Sorry" and Love Yourself."But this seems like the right time — 11:25 p.m. on Saturday, April 11, to be exact — for the singer to take the stage.After several years of constant media attention, Bieber recently took time away from the stage due to his health. That break, in turn, proved to be productive as he released "Swag" and "Swag II" last year, giving us an intimate look into his domestic life and how his musicality has matured since his teenage years. Bieber's headlining performance has the potential to be one of the most talked about and memorable sets from not just this festival, but of the decade.There's still much to wonder about his set, but some recent live appearances have given us some clues for what to expect. Bieber will take the Coachella stage Saturday, April 11, with the first weekend of the festival taking place Friday, April 10 through Sunday, April 12 at the Empire Polo Club in Indio.Past Coachella appearances draw excitementThough the 2026 festival marks the first time Bieber has been on the lineup, it's not the first time he's performed at Coachella.Some of the artists he's guested with include Chance the Rapper in 2014 for the song "Confident"; 2019 headliner Ariana Grande to sing his hit "Sorry"; Daniel Caesar and Giveon in 2022 for a performance of "Peaches"; and Tems and Wizkid for the song "Essence."Each time he's appeared, the crowd's love and passion for him has been clear. Cheers and screams can be heard throughout the Empire Polo Club, signaling a superstar is in people's midst. Not to mention, Bieber's vocal chops only continue to get stronger and more soulful.Aside from on-stage appearances, Bieber has been a staple among the Coachella grounds. Fans have spotted him dancing with his wife, Hailey, hanging out with friends and even making Billie Eilish's dreams come true by meeting in person. However, it's also been reported that he punched a man in 2018 for choking a woman at an after party in La Quinta, so you never really know what you'll get with him.Why Coachella 2026 is the right time for Justin Bieber to headlineSome fans might think Coachella organizers missed an opportunity in the 2010s to have Bieber on its lineup. "Bieber Fever" was all the rage then, and he consistently came out with chart-topping songs.But I reckon the Bieber we see on stage Saturday knows more about himself, the music he wants to put out and the show he wants to deliver than the Bieber we would have gotten a decade ago.The 2020s have seen a lot of change in Bieber's life. He and Hailey became parents in 2024, welcoming a son, and that has had a profound impact on the singer's personal life and work. It can be heard in his albums "Swag" and "Swag II," in which he explores married life and his journey into fatherhood. "When you take my hand, honey, I promise you just tenderness/Pull me out when you come in, and you turn me to a better man," he sings on "Better Man." In the song "Mother in You," Bieber croons about seeing so much of himself and his wife in their child with the lyrics, "My smile, her grace, both of our hearts."Those records have also shown the way he's matured when it comes to his music. Long gone are the ultra-poppy songs from his breakout years. Instead, listeners now get R&B and indie sounds with smooth vocals and infectious beats that paint vivid images.The 32-year-old has also been open about health struggles, addiction and the burden of fame over the years. At times, we've seen his more challenging moments — like when he clashed with paparazzi in Indio last year — but it's also humanized this figure who has been in the spotlight for nearly two decades now.What to expect from Justin Bieber's headlining setThe big question remains: What is Bieber going to do when he hits the stage on Saturday? While we won't know for sure until his set begins, we've gotten some clues in recent weeks.The singer took the Grammy Awards stage in February — four years after his last performance of "Peaches" at the award show — and delivered a stripped-down version of "Yukon" from "Swag." He stepped out in lavender boxer shorts, black socks and a guitar, and while many artists opted for flashy production design, he was alone on stage with his music production equipment. Utilizing a looping station, Bieber built up the beat for his song before he let his soulful vocals take center stage.Throughout the performance, the singer kept his eyes closed and his hands close to his body, not at all acknowledging the crowd in front of him.It was a great reintroduction to the singer, who has taken a lengthy hiatus from performing after being diagnosed with Ramsay Hunt syndrome, which can cause facial weakness/paralysis. The Grammys set also showed that he doesn't need much to bring in an audience. Whenever the camera panned out into the crowd, people were captivated by the music and vibe he set.There's also the question of whether he'll stick to just his most recent work, or if he'll do a whole retrospective performance with some of his earlier hits at Coachella. In recent invite-only Los Angeles shows at The Roxy and Troubadour venues, the singer has opted for "Swag" and "Swag II" tracks, which leads many to believe they might not hear "Baby" after all.It's worth noting that Bieber sold his publishing and recorded music rights in 2022 for more than $200 million. The deal included his entire back catalog, totaling 290 songs released before Dec. 31, 2021. It's not clear if the sale would bar the singer from performing any of those songs, but we have a feeling he'd be allowed to sing them (it is Coachella, after all).Though there's many questions and speculation surrounding this performance, there's one thing we know to be true: Tens of thousands of festivalgoers will gather around the Coachella Stage to take in this decades-in-the-making performance.What day is Justin Bieber performing at Coachella?Saturday, April 11 and Saturday, April 18. Only Weekend 1 set times have been released so far, and for Weekend 1, his set will begin at 11:25 p.m.Coachella 2026 lineupWant to see who else is on this year's festival lineup?
